reason: The verdict holds: this does not reach the bar and belongs on the post-deadline list. I checked the facts. (1) The premise is right. FACTS F-DAT-12 says DeepCenter was trained only on the 71 44b6 clips and selected on 6bba. (2) The public asymmetry is right. dc0.30 (probe 41) = 0.949, -0.005 vs K2, with forks 75 -> 55. dc0.20 (43) and dc0.225 (44) both = 0.954, with 96 and 88 forks, and 0 teams passed, so no UP (CONTEXT 04:58Z and 13:14Z). So the DC band is the most sensitive public division term, and it is sensitive only on the harmful side. (3) There is no DC trainer. A grep of tools/ and experiments/ finds only the B32 division-pair runner, which uses DC as a veto input. The weights are a third-party pack with an unknown recipe. The finding also misses a stronger feasibility point. Training on both embryos uses up 6bba, the only honest bed for checkpoint selection and threshold calibration. The 0.25 threshold would then be applied to a shifted score distribution with no honest gate at all. Only a LOEO scheme (I-368) would be honest, and it costs about 2x the GPU. On the rules: R8 passed at 12:00Z. The user's lifts cover exp72, E10 v3 ports and division-side public rungs, not a new DC model, so this would need a new OK. The GPU queue is also congested (the exp75 dummy has been QUEUED since 13:18Z), and the 28 Sep slots are already routed (exp72, exp75, then by the 45/46 reads). The value is weak too. The retrain family is 0 for 5 on the LB, and a DC shift acts like an uncalibrated threshold rung whose public downside (-0.005) is bigger than its demonstrated upside (0). So P(+0.002) ~0.10 looks generous; ~0.05 is more realistic. Minor: '0.20/0.225 showed 0' means a tie within the display bin, not a measured zero.
